- If we use the classifier endpoint instead of the re-ranker for a cheaper path (binary accept/reject per candidate), how does that change the billing model?
- Any recommended batching or KV-cache approaches for our pattern to reduce cost?

Hi Olivia — great context, thanks for the spreadsheet. High-level answers below and a worked example at the end. I've attached our relevance-specific rate card PDF for reference.

TL;DR: For the hosted API we price relevance workloads as a combination of (1) per-scoring-unit fees and (2) optional token-based context charges for long candidates. This avoids charging per full model-generation token while giving predictable unit economics for dense scoring loops.

How we bill (baseline hosted pricing):
- Scoring unit: charged per candidate scored. Default baseline: $0.0009 per candidate scored for the Re-ranker endpoint (cross-attention scoring).
- Classifier endpoint: cheaper per-candidate evaluation when you can run a single forward pass per candidate — baseline $0.00035 per candidate.
- Context/token surcharge: when your candidate/context size exceeds 512 tokens combined, we apply a small per-token surcharge ($0.00002 per token) to account for attention/memory cost.
- Request overhead: a tiny per-request routing fee ($0.00005) for bookkeeping and headers.

Discounts / commits:
- Pilot: 12% one-time introductory credit for the first 90 days (applies to scoring unit fees).
- Volume tiers: 5% at $10k/mo; 12% at $50k/mo; 18% custom for >$150k/mo (enterprise).

Worked example (your numbers):
- 5k queries/day * 100 candidates = 500k candidates/day -> ~15M candidates/month.
- If you use the Re-ranker: 15M * $0.0009 = $13,500/mo before discounts.
- Token surcharge estimate (median candidate ~60 tokens, context ~30 tokens -> 90 total <512 so surcharge is negligible). If some candidates are long and average 800 tokens, token surcharge would be (800-512)=288 extra tokens * $0.00002 * 15M = $86,400/mo (so we recommend trimming candidate size or using embeddings + classifier where sensible).
- Classifier path: 15M * $0.00035 = $5,250/mo — tradeoff: simpler scoring, less contextual cross-attention quality.

Cost optimization suggestions:
- Use the classifier for initial filtering (cheap per-candidate) then re-rank top-N (N=20) with the cross-attention re-ranker. Example: classifier 100 candidates -> keep 20 -> re-rank 20. That pattern reduces re-ranker candidate counts by 5x.
- Enable automatic batching (we can batch across customers/session windows) — typical 8–12% unit cost improvement.
- Prefix KV cache: if you have stable prefixes across queries, cache candidate encodings to avoid repeated token surcharges.

Next steps: I'll add a tailored cost model spreadsheet and the attached rate_card_relevance_v1.pdf. If you can share a short list of peak candidate sizes or an example query stream, we can give a line-by-line estimate.

Best,
Camila Reyes
